RAK1906 is a WisBlock Sensor that is based on the popular BOSCH BME680 environment sensor chip which monitors environmental air quality. A ready to use SW library and tutorial makes it easy to build up motion data acquisition system. RAK1906 is not only measuring air temperature, humidity, and barometric pressure. It has as well an integrated gas sensor to acquire information about air quality. RAK1906 combined with the RAK4631 WisBlock Core is ready to go system for air quality and condition system. It's use cases are personal air quality tracker, weather stations, or gas detection, The acquired data can be send using LoRaWan® communication, LoRa® point to point connections, and BLE. RAK1906 is ideal for battery-powered applications because of its low power consumption. In addition, the WisBlock system allows to power down the module complete to reduce the power consumption of the system even more. RAK1904 is a WisBlock Sensor based on STMicroelectronics LIS3DH chip which extends the WisBlock system to have a 3-axis acceleration sensing capabilities. WisMesh High Power Booster Starter Kit brings more Tx power and better reception to Meshtastic networks. Powered by the RAK3401 WisBlock Core module with the Nordic nRF52840 MCU and a RAK13302 High Power LoRa transceiver module, mounted on a RAK19007 Base Board. Unlike common solutions, the RAK13302 integrates a dedicated RF filter stage, which not only enables high-power transmission but also significantly enhances receiver sensitivity. This means longer range, more stable links, and stronger mesh reliability. This is ideal for outdoor adventures, emergency communications, or wide-area IoT coverage, positioning it as some of the best hardware for long-range Meshtastic networks. Notes: Transmit power limits and allowable frequency plans differ by country and region. This product supports high power operation, but users must configure transmit power, antenna gain, and frequency settings to comply with local regulations. There are two variants of the RAK13302 LoRa module that have different power requirements: (116256 Battery Powered) - The booster module gets all of its power from the JST 2.0 Battery Port on the RAK19007 Base Board. A battery is required for this setup. USB and Solar work to charge the battery. This variant works best for solar repeaters/mobile nodes. (116257 External 5V Powered) - The booster module requires a 5V power input using the connector on the underside of the RAK13302 module. You will also need to power the RAK3400 Core Module using either USB-C or Battery Power. This variant works best for deployments with stable grid-based power supplies. The RAK13302 module features hardware capable of higher Tx power than traditional radios, enabled by the integrated Skyworks SKY66122 power amplifier. This device is FCC-certified (FCC ID: 2AF6B-13302) for a maximum conducted output power of 290 mW (approximately 24.6 dBm) in the United States. 290mw is almost 3x the power of most standard LoRa and Meshtastic radios, so there will be a noticeable improvement in Tx power and transmit distance at FCC approved settings. Under FCC rules, operation of this device in the United States must not exceed the power levels authorized under its FCC grant of certification. Devices will ship with compliant power settings. Why choose the WisMesh High Power Booster Starter Kit for your Meshtastic network? Whether upgrading a Meshtastic High Power node or building a fresh deployment, this kit is engineered specifically for users who need reliable, long-range mesh communication in off-grid, outdoor, or emergency setups. The use of the nRF52840 MCU ensures modern BLE and firmware compatibility, while the WisBlock modular ecosystem allows you to expand with sensors, displays, trackers, or repeater nodes with ease. Compared to typical Meshtastic kits (~100 mw output) our DIY High Power builds (which may lack RF filtering or stability), this kit delivers a proven, stable high-power solution—all while managing power, heat and regulatory concerns in a single product. Key Features WisBlock RAK3401 Core module Nordic nRF52840 MCU ARM Cortex-M4F 1MB Flash and 348KB SRAM I/O ports: UART/I2C/SPI/ADC/GPIO WisBlock RAK13302 LoRa transceiver module (FCC limit 290mW) Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver SKY66122 signal booster Integrated RF filter for enhanced reception performance IPEX antenna connector for LoRa Support for 9xx MHz frequency band RAK19007 WisBlock Base Board 4 sensor slots for WisBlock Sensor Modules Supply voltage 5V over USB 5V over Solar Panel connector Rechargeable battery Range & RF Performance: SX1262 + SKY66122 Amplified Path The WisMesh High Power Booster Starter Kit delivers exceptional performance for users needing a long-range Meshtastic solution. This is done by combining the Semtech SX1262 LoRa transceiver with the Skyworks SKY66122 high-power amplifier and a dedicated SAW filter. Unlike typical high-power boards that boost TX but degrade RX, this filtered RF chain, including an RF filter and PA for improved receiver sensitivity, preserves receiver performance while increasing output power. The result is a cleaner signal, reduced self-interference, and significantly stronger SNR across real-world deployments. Users can expect more reliable two-way links, improved packet retention at long distances, and stable mesh coverage even in semi-obstructed environments. Power Requirements & Thermal Notes The High Power RF stage in the RAK13302 demands a stable 5V supply, as 3.3V sources cannot deliver the surge current required for high-power LoRa transmission. For reliable operation, users should power the module through USB, a regulated 5V adapter, or the WisBlock Base Board’s battery system—especially when using an SX1262 LoRa module in continuous or high-duty-cycle deployments. How the High Power RF Chain Works (nRF52840 → SX1262 → PA/Filter) The WisMesh High Power Booster Starter Kit uses a staged RF architecture to deliver clean, long-range LoRa performance. The nRF52840 MCU manages firmware and communicates with the SX1262 transceiver, which generates the sub-GHz LoRa signal, making the architecture suitable for a nRF52840 Meshtastic deployment. That signal is then boosted by the SKY66122 power amplifier, a SKY66122 LoRa amplifier module, and passed through an integrated SAW filter to remove noise and harmonics. This ensures both high transmit power and excellent receiver sensitivity, enabling stable two-way communication even at long distances, as shown in the diagram below. WisMesh High Power Booster Starter Kit brings more Tx power and better reception to Meshtastic networks. Powered by the RAK3401 WisBlock Core module with the Nordic nRF52840 MCU and a RAK13302 High Power LoRa transceiver module, mounted on a RAK19007 Base Board. Unlike common solutions, the RAK13302 integrates a dedicated RF filter stage, which not only enables high-power transmission but also significantly enhances receiver sensitivity. This means longer range, more stable links, and stronger mesh reliability. This is ideal for outdoor adventures, emergency communications, or wide-area IoT coverage, positioning it as some of the best hardware for long-range Meshtastic networks. Notes: Transmit power limits and allowable frequency plans differ by country and region. This product supports high power operation, but users must configure transmit power, antenna gain, and frequency settings to comply with local regulations. There are two variants of the RAK13302 LoRa module that have different power requirements: (116256 Battery Powered) - The booster module gets all of its power from the JST 2.0 Battery Port on the RAK19007 Base Board. A battery is required for this setup. USB and Solar work to charge the battery. This variant works best for solar repeaters/mobile nodes. (116257 External 5V Powered) - The booster module requires a 5V power input using the connector on the underside of the RAK13302 module. You will also need to power the RAK3400 Core Module using either USB-C or Battery Power. This variant works best for deployments with stable grid-based power supplies. The RAK13302 module features hardware capable of higher Tx power than traditional radios, enabled by the integrated Skyworks SKY66122 power amplifier. This device is FCC-certified (FCC ID: 2AF6B-13302) for a maximum conducted output power of 290 mW (approximately 24.6 dBm) in the United States. 290mw is almost 3x the power of most standard LoRa and Meshtastic radios, so there will be a noticeable improvement in Tx power and transmit distance at FCC approved settings. Under FCC rules, operation of this device in the United States must not exceed the power levels authorized under its FCC grant of certification. Devices will ship with compliant power settings. RAK5802 is a WisBlock RS485 interface module based on TP8485 from 3PEAK that extends the WisBlock system with an industrial RS485 data transmission interface. A ready-to-use SW library and tutorial makes it easy to connect any sensor that is using the RS485 interface. RAK5802 supports one RS485 interface and has a battery and 3.3V power output to supply sensors. In addition, an I2C interface connection is available on the crimping terminal. RAK5802 combined with the RAK4631 WisBlock Core gives your solution for an interface to industrial sensors and actuators that support the RS485 interface. This interface is the bridge between such sensors and LoRaWan® communication, LoRa® point to point connections or BLE. RAK5802 is ideal for battery-powered applications because of its low power consumption. In addition, the WisBlock system allows to power down the module completely to reduce the power consumption of the system even more. The RAK12501 WisBlock GNSS Location Tracker Module uses the Quectel L76K and is designed to be part of a production-ready IoT solution in a modular way. It must be combined with a WisBlock Base board and core module to work as an LPWAN tracker device.Use with Meshtastic- compatible with RAK Meshtastic Starter Kit and Starter Kit Mini versions. The RAK12501 supports a wide variety of satellite data protocols, such as GPS, GLONASS, QZSS, and BeiDou. This ensures the retrieval of precise location data. It works with standard protocols over UART connection to the MCU. Track your assets, devices, or outdoor sensors with high-precision GNSS using the cost-effective RAK12501 module. It’s built for Meshtastic GPS tracker projects and other LPWAN-based solutions, offering accurate location data without breaking the bank. GNSS antenna How to Get Started with WisBlock RAK12501 GNSS Module RAK12501 Quick Start Guide RAK12501 Datasheet WisBlock Quick Start Guide WisBlock Source Code Repository(opens new window)(opens new window) 24-Pin Male Connector 3D File(opens new window) WisBlock Sensor Tutorial Frequently Asked Questions What is the RAK12501 GNSS Module used for? The RAK12501 is used to track the location of devices in IoT projects. It receives satellite signals and calculates precise geographic coordinates. It’s ideal for low-power LPWAN applications like Meshtastic trackers, asset monitoring, or outdoor sensors. Why does the RAK12501 only support UART and not I2C? The RAK12501 is designed around the Quectel L76K module, which supports UART communication only (unlike RAK12500, which supports both UART and I2C). This simplifies the hardware interface and is sufficient for serial GNSS data exchange using NMEA 0183 protocol. Compared to I2C, UART is often easier to implement and debug for IoT GPS modules with continuous data streams. How do I connect the RAK12501 to a WisBlock Core? To use the RAK12501, you’ll need a WisBlock Base and a WisBlock Core. Plug the RAK12501 into a slot on the WisBlock Base Board that supports UART. Make sure your WisBlock Core Use the UART pins defined by the WisBlock Base to read GNSS data via NMEA sentences. In your firmware, set up UART communication and parse the NMEA data for position information. How fast does the RAK12501 get a satellite fix? The RAK12501 features very fast startup times: Cold start: under 15 seconds Warm start: under 5 seconds Hot start: under 1 second This ensures you get location data quickly, even after powering down. Can I use the RAK12501 in battery-powered projects? Yes, the RAK12501 is built for low-power applications. It uses only 7µA in backup mode and 18–25mA during tracking or acquisition, making it a great choice for portable or long-deployment devices.
